quests.instruction: Which vehicle does a family often keep at home for trips to the shops?
quests.hint: It has four wheels, drives on the road, and has room for a few people.
quests.explanation: A car has four wheels and a motor, and it drives on roads. Many families use one for short trips like shopping or visiting friends.
quests.funFact: Some cars today run on electricity from a battery instead of petrol or diesel.

quests.instruction: Which road vehicle has lots of seats and stops at bus stops so many people can ride together?
quests.hint: Look for the long vehicle that waits at a stop for a whole line of people.
quests.explanation: A bus carries many passengers at once, so people can share one vehicle instead of each using a separate car. It follows a route and stops along the way.
quests.funFact: London's famous red double-decker buses have seats on two floors.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle runs on metal rails and is made of a long line of connected carriages?
quests.hint: Its wheels are made for rails, not for roads.
quests.explanation: A train travels on a railway track made of metal rails. Its connected carriages can carry many passengers or heavy goods.
quests.funFact: Some high-speed trains travel faster than 300 kilometres per hour.

quests.instruction: Which huge vehicle sails across the ocean carrying passengers or cargo?
quests.hint: It is so big that it can travel far from land, much bigger than a boat on a lake.
quests.explanation: A ship is a very large vessel built to cross seas and oceans. Some ships carry passengers, while others carry cargo like cars, fruit, and toys.
quests.funFact: Some container ships carry thousands of metal boxes full of goods.

quests.instruction: Which small boat zooms across a lake because it has a motor at the back?
quests.hint: Listen for the engine. It is much smaller and quicker than a ship.
quests.explanation: A speedboat uses a motor to turn a propeller under the water. The spinning propeller pushes the boat forward fast.
quests.funFact: Speedboats are often used by rescue teams because they can reach people quickly.

quests.instruction: Which boat moves when a person pulls two long oars through the water?
quests.hint: Muscles do the work here. There is no engine and no sail.
quests.explanation: A rowboat is moved by oars. Pulling the oars pushes water backwards, which makes the boat glide forward.
quests.funFact: Rowers sit facing backwards, so they see where they have been, not where they are going.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle has two wheels and moves when you push its pedals round with your feet?
quests.hint: Look for a seat, handlebars, and a chain turned by your own legs.
quests.explanation: A bicycle has two wheels and pedals. When you push the pedals, a chain turns the back wheel and the bicycle rolls along.
quests.funFact: A bicycle needs no fuel at all, only your own energy.

quests.instruction: Which two-wheeled vehicle roars along because it has an engine?
quests.hint: Pedals are not what make it go. Listen for the noise.
quests.explanation: A motorcycle has two wheels like a bicycle, but an engine does the work. Riders wear a helmet to protect their heads.
quests.funFact: In many countries, the law says motorcycle riders must wear helmets.

quests.instruction: Which small vehicle do you ride standing up, steering with handlebars while pushing off with one foot?
quests.hint: You stand on a little board with a handle to hold, and one foot kicks the ground.
quests.explanation: A kick scooter has small wheels, a board to stand on, and handlebars to steer. You kick the ground with one foot to roll forward.
quests.funFact: Many kick scooters fold up so they are easy to carry.

quests.instruction: Which strong vehicle carries boxes and heavy goods in a big space at the back?
quests.hint: Think of a vehicle that brings goods to shops rather than people.
quests.explanation: A truck is built to carry goods such as food, furniture, and parcels. Its large back area holds much more than a car can.
quests.funFact: Some trucks are refrigerated, so their cargo stays cold on long trips.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle with huge back wheels pulls farm machines across muddy fields?
quests.hint: Its big, chunky wheels are made to grip soft soil.
quests.explanation: A tractor is a strong farm vehicle. Its big tyres grip muddy ground, and it can pull ploughs and trailers.
quests.funFact: Some tractor tyres are taller than an adult.

quests.instruction: Which car, often with a sign on its roof, can be hired to take you where you want to go?
quests.hint: The driver works for passengers, and you pay for the ride at the end.
quests.explanation: A taxi is a car with a driver that you can hire for a trip. You tell the driver where to go and pay a fare.
quests.funFact: New York City's taxis are famously bright yellow.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle races to a fire carrying ladders, hoses, and firefighters?
quests.hint: Look for the vehicle that carries water and long hoses.
quests.explanation: A fire engine carries firefighters and the tools they need to put out fires and rescue people.
quests.funFact: In some countries, fire engines are bright yellow or lime-green so they are easy to see.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle uses a siren and flashing lights to take a hurt person to hospital?
quests.hint: Trained medical helpers ride inside, and there is a bed for patients.
quests.explanation: An ambulance carries paramedics and medical equipment. They can start helping a sick or hurt person on the way to hospital.
quests.funFact: Air ambulances are helicopters that fly patients to hospital.

quests.instruction: Which car do police officers drive to patrol the streets and respond to danger?
quests.hint: It has special lights, and the people inside work to keep everyone safe.
quests.explanation: A police car carries officers who help people and keep roads and neighbourhoods safe. Its lights and siren warn others to make way.
quests.funFact: Some police teams also patrol on bicycles, boats, and horses.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle runs on rails set into a city street and gets power from wires overhead?
quests.hint: It looks like a short train but shares the street with traffic.
quests.explanation: A tram runs on rails built into the road and uses electricity from overhead wires. Trams carry people around busy parts of cities.
quests.funFact: Melbourne in Australia has one of the biggest tram networks in the world.

quests.instruction: Which train zooms through tunnels beneath a busy city, far below the traffic?
quests.hint: Look for the one that hides below the streets.
quests.explanation: A subway, or metro, is a train that runs mostly underground. Staying below the streets lets it avoid traffic and carry lots of people quickly.
quests.funFact: London's Underground opened in 1863 and is the world's oldest underground railway.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle hangs from a strong cable and carries people up a steep mountain?
quests.hint: It does not roll on the ground. It is held up high by something above.
quests.explanation: A cable car hangs from strong cables and is pulled up and down steep slopes. It helps people reach places where roads would be too steep.
quests.funFact: Some cable cars carry skiers and hikers high above deep valleys.

quests.instruction: Which boat has a tall sail that catches the wind to push it along?
quests.hint: Look for the big piece of cloth that fills up and pulls the boat.
quests.explanation: A sailboat uses the wind. When wind fills the sail, it pushes the boat across the water without needing fuel.
quests.funFact: Sailors have used wind power to cross oceans for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which boat carries cars and passengers across a river or bay on regular trips?
quests.hint: Cars can drive right on and off, a bit like a floating bridge.
quests.explanation: A ferry carries people, and often cars, from one shore to another on a regular schedule.
quests.funFact: Some ferries carry hundreds of cars and trucks at once.

quests.instruction: Which long, narrow boat do you move by dipping a paddle into the water?
quests.hint: People sit or kneel low and pull a paddle through the water.
quests.explanation: A canoe is a light, narrow boat. Paddling pushes water backwards and moves the canoe forward.
quests.funFact: People around the world have used canoes for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which flying vehicle has spinning blades on top and can hover in one spot?
quests.hint: It does not need a long runway. It can go straight up and down.
quests.explanation: A helicopter's spinning blades lift it into the air. This lets it hover and land in small spaces, so it is useful for rescues.
quests.funFact: Helicopters can fly backwards and sideways as well as forwards.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle blasts upwards with a huge fire-tail to travel into space?
quests.hint: It has to leave the sky behind and go much, much higher.
quests.explanation: A rocket's powerful engines push it upwards so fast that it can leave Earth's air behind and reach space.
quests.funFact: To orbit Earth, a rocket must reach about 28,000 kilometres per hour.

quests.instruction: Which flying vehicle has wings and needs a long runway at an airport to take off?
quests.hint: The wings and a long strip of ground help it lift off.
quests.explanation: An airplane speeds along a runway until its wings lift it into the air. Airplanes carry passengers and cargo across long distances.
quests.funFact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only 12 seconds.

quests.instruction: Which flat board with four small wheels do you ride standing up, with no handlebars?
quests.hint: You balance on it and lean to steer.
quests.explanation: A skateboard is a board with four wheels. Riders push off with one foot and lean to turn.
quests.funFact: Skateboarding is now an Olympic sport.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle slides over snow on flat runners instead of wheels?
quests.hint: Wheels would sink into the snow, so this has smooth strips underneath.
quests.explanation: A sled has flat runners that glide easily over snow and ice. It works in places where wheels would get stuck.
quests.funFact: People in snowy regions have used dog sleds to travel for a very long time.

quests.instruction: Which small three-wheeled vehicle is a popular taxi in many busy towns, with a roof but open sides?
quests.hint: Count its wheels. It has one fewer than a car.
quests.explanation: An auto rickshaw has three wheels and a small engine. It is narrow and light, so it can weave through busy streets with a few passengers.
quests.funFact: In Thailand, auto rickshaws are often called tuk-tuks.

quests.instruction: Which old-fashioned train puffs steam out of a tall chimney?
quests.hint: It burns fuel to boil water and make steam.
quests.explanation: A steam locomotive heats water to make steam, and the steam pushes parts that turn the wheels. These were common before modern electric and diesel trains.
quests.funFact: Some old steam trains still carry visitors on special heritage railways.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle has a car-style front and an open space at the back for carrying things?
quests.hint: Look for a vehicle that is half car and half open box.
quests.explanation: A pickup truck has a cab for people at the front and an open bed at the back, handy for tools, plants, or farm supplies.
quests.funFact: Pickup trucks are very common on farms and building sites.

quests.instruction: Which very big truck pulls a long trailer along highways?
quests.hint: The front part and the long back part are joined together, and it is bigger than a delivery truck.
quests.explanation: An articulated truck has a cab that pulls a long trailer. It carries large loads over long distances on highways.
quests.funFact: In North America, these trucks are often called 18-wheelers because they usually have eighteen wheels.
